title: Accept partial requests; stop only on malformed input
story: As a requester, I want to submit what I know now, so that I am asked for the rest instead of being rejected.
acceptance: Missing answers become questions, not errors; a malformed date or non-numeric value stops with the field name; an email address as requester id is refused

title: Category from the requester, or inferred and confirmed
story: As a requester, I want the agent to work out the category from my description, so that I do not need to know procurement categories.
acceptance: A valid chosen category is used as is; otherwise a unique keyword match is proposed for the requester to confirm; a tie or no match becomes a question listing the options

title: Method from procurement-owned thresholds, with the rule shown
story: As a procurement officer, I want every recommended method to show the rule, value and threshold, so that I can check it in seconds.
acceptance: Method comes from config/policy.json, never from code; the rule names the method, the value used and the threshold band; boundary values fall in the higher band

title: Reuse first: framework agreement call-off
story: As a procurement officer, I want requests covered by an active framework agreement routed to a call-off, so that we do not run competitions we already ran.
acceptance: An active framework for the category with enough ceiling is found; covered scope -> call-off recommended; uncertain scope -> 'officer to confirm'; expired or exhausted frameworks are ignored

title: Split-purchase guard on the 12-month total
story: As a procurement officer, I want related requests from the same unit and category counted, so that a large need is not split under a threshold.
acceptance: Same unit, same category, last 12 months, not cancelled are added; the method is set on the total; a SPLIT flag explains both methods when they differ

title: Named supplier needs a justification
story: As a procurement officer, I want a named supplier on a competitive method to come with a justification, so that sole sourcing is a decision, not a default.
acceptance: Named supplier + competitive method + no framework -> SOLE flag; missing justification is a required item with a question; direct purchase and framework call-offs do not trigger it

title: TOR draft from the template, nothing invented
story: As a requester, I want a TOR drafted from my answers, so that I start from a document, not a blank page.
acceptance: Every template section is present in order; unknowns are marked [TO CONFIRM]; every number and date in the draft appears in the request or is a policy reference

title: Completeness checklist and questions
story: As a procurement officer, I want incomplete requests to come back as questions before they reach me, so that my first review is my only review.
acceptance: Each required item is met or carries one plain question; the case is 'Needs information' while any required item is unmet; recommended items never block

title: Human checkpoints and four eyes
story: As the head of procurement, I want only named people in named roles to move a case forward, so that the agent can never approve spend.
acceptance: Agent role cannot confirm, approve or return; only the submitting requester confirms; requester cannot decide on own request; only ids on the procurement-owned role roster can decide; approving a case with an attention flag needs a note; at or above the sign-off threshold, officer then a different budget holder; returns need a note

title: Request text is data, never instructions
story: As the head of procurement, I want instruction-like text in a request flagged and withheld, so that nobody can steer the agent through a form field.
acceptance: Instruction-like text is flagged per field as blocking; the field is withheld from the draft; method, routing and status are unchanged by it; the case cannot reach an officer until rewritten

title: Officer package with audit trail
story: As a procurement officer, I want one package with the draft, flags, checklist and what the agent did and why, so that I can review without opening an email thread.
acceptance: Markdown, HTML (light and dark) and JSON are produced for every case; the audit trail lists each tool call with its reason and result; decisions by people are listed separately

title: Usage events for the adoption tracker
story: As the product owner, I want usage events in the ai-adoption-tracker format, so that the pilot's scale-or-stop review rests on evidence.
acceptance: One task_completed per confirmed request and one feedback event per rating; user ids are pseudonymous requester ids; columns date,use_case_id,user_id,action

title: Model-assisted TOR wording with a fact validator
story: As a requester, I want the draft to read like a finished TOR, so that I edit less.
acceptance: A model may rephrase confirmed answers only; a validator rejects any number, date, name or commitment not in the request; on rejection the template text is kept; token cap per request

title: Conversational intake in the collaboration platform
story: As a requester, I want to answer the questions in chat, so that I do not fill a form.
acceptance: Same questions as the checklist, asked one at a time; answers saved to the request; resumable; the agent's powers unchanged

title: Officer queue with ageing and service levels
story: As a procurement team lead, I want each queue sorted by age with the service level shown, so that nothing waits unseen.
acceptance: Queue view by age and readiness; breach of the agreed review time highlighted; no personal data beyond pseudonymous ids

title: Cycle-time and rework measures
story: As the product owner, I want submission-to-approval time and returns per case measured, so that the value case uses measured numbers.
acceptance: Cycle time and number of returns per case computed from case history; baseline period comparable; shown in the pilot report

title: Catalogue and past-purchase reuse
story: As a requester, I want to see when a similar purchase was made recently, so that I can reuse its TOR or supplier route.
acceptance: Past requests with similar title and category listed with their outcome; reuse is a suggestion, never automatic

title: Model planner behind the same policy engine
story: As the head of procurement, I want any model-driven planning to stay inside the same tools and checkpoints, so that autonomy grows only where evidence supports it.
acceptance: Planner swaps behind the same interface; same regression set passes; planted injections still flagged; no new tools or permissions
